Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a matching 40 fps cap is the sweet spot for this game on Deck — smoother than 30 fps and more sustainable than 60 fps. FSR upscaling from 960x600 recovers image quality while keeping the GPU load manageable during chaotic team fights.

profiles.Summary: Marvel Rivals is a demanding Unreal Engine 5 hero shooter that pushes the Steam Deck hard — expect 30–40 fps at low settings with FSR upscaling, as the game's minimum GPU spec (GTX 1060/RX 580) already exceeds the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU capability. The game is rated Playable on Deck with gold-tier ProtonDB reports, so it runs but requires significant settings cuts and upscaling to stay smooth in team fights.
profiles.BasisNote: No dedicated Steam Deck or Linux player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1060/RX 580, which exceeds the Deck's GPU) and Deck hardware capabilities. On your first session, check the frame rate in a full 6v6 team fight — if it drops below 28 fps consistently in the Optimal profile, switch to Max Battery settings and lower render resolution further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 848x530 and let Deck FSR upscale to 1280x800 for maximum headroom; the 8 W TDP and 900 MHz GPU clock keep heat and fan noise low for longer sessions. Drop to 30 Hz refresh to perfectly match the frame cap and reduce judder.

KnownIssues: Anti-cheat (EQU8/Ricochet) compatibility may cause launch issues on some Proton versions — try Proton Experimental or GE-Proton if the game fails to start
Frame pacing can be inconsistent during large team fights and ultimate abilities, causing brief stutters even with a frame cap
The game's online requirement means network latency adds to perceived input lag on the Deck's lower frame rates
In-game text and UI elements can be small on the 7-inch 1280x800 screen, especially at upscaled resolutions

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full 15 W TDP with GPU at max clock extracts the most frames possible, but expect dips into the low 40s during heavy team-fight ultimates — a 45 fps cap prevents the GPU from chasing unattainable highs and keeps frame pacing stable. Battery life is short; keep a charger nearby.

Optimal.Notes: The 40 fps cap synced to 40 Hz refresh gives perfectly smooth pacing for a competitive shooter; FSR from 1024x640 keeps image quality acceptable while the GPU clock at 1200 MHz provides headroom for busier team fights.

profiles.Summary: Marvel Rivals is a demanding hero shooter that sits above the Steam Deck's GPU class at minimum spec, so expect 30–40 fps at low settings with FSR upscaling; the game is playable but not silky-smooth. ProtonDB reporters rate it gold, meaning it runs with minor issues under Proton, and the free-to-play online nature means a stable internet connection is required at all times.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1060 minimum, well above the Deck's ~GTX 1050 Ti class GPU) and general Deck hardware capability. On first launch, check frame rate in a full 6v6 team fight — if it drops below 28 fps consistently on Optimal, drop to Max Battery settings, and if it holds 50+ fps, try nudging Effects Quality to Medium.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and let Deck FSR upscale to 1280x800 to ease GPU load; the 8 W TDP and locked 900 MHz GPU clock keep heat and power draw minimal for longer sessions.

KnownIssues: Anti-cheat (EQU8/Easy Anti-Cheat) may cause launch failures on some Proton versions — try Proton Experimental or GE-Proton if the game won't start.
Online-only PvP means any network hiccup causes disconnection regardless of local settings.
Shader compilation stutters are common on first launch and in new areas until the shader cache is built.
In-game text and UI elements can be very small at 1280x800; increasing UI scale in settings is recommended.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Uncapping TDP lets the APU boost freely for the best possible frame rate, but expect dips into the mid-40s during large team fights; battery life will be short and the deck will run warm, so this is best for docked or plugged-in play.
